purpose: Bounded ROM-read sequencing experiment for the track-table progression question

observations.interpretation: Two copy loops read the same selected ROM table in ascending order; the trace is split across frames.
A later runtime pass also marches forward through the selected table rather than using an indexed per-frame cursor.
The transition/update pass again reads a contiguous prefix from the table.
The copy loops repeat the contiguous 384-word table march after the transition.
A later progression interval selects the 0x044930 ROM slot and reads it sequentially.
The same 0x044930 slot is revisited by another contiguous runtime pass.

supported: Observed table loads are sequential contiguous ROM marches with a 16-bit (0x2-byte) source stride.
The copy path uses fixed 0x300-byte / 384-word table extents when fully observed.
The recorded race reuses ROM slots across progression intervals; it does not show a single distance cursor walking one ever-advancing ROM address.
unresolved: The exact semantic meaning of each table word or record remains unknown.
This capture does not by itself prove whether a later geometry consumer indexes the copied RAM buffer per scanline or segment.
The progression-state-to-slot selection remains a finite table lookup, not a decoded track-number formula.
